title: Åre: Sweden's Lift-Linked Winter Capital

bestPeriod.window: Early December to early May. **March and April** are the best weeks, long light, deep base, spring sun and the resort's biggest events; February is coldest and reliably snowy; December is dark but festive
bestPeriod.raw: Early December to early May. **March and April** are the best weeks, long light, deep base, spring sun and the resort's biggest events; February is coldest and reliably snowy; December is dark but festive

accommodation.note: €140-280 per night for an apartment sleeping 4; hotel doubles €160-300; ski-in/ski-out mountain lodges €300+

food.note: €60-100 per day; apartment self-catering roughly halves it

transport.note: €200-350: night train Stockholm-Åre (the station is in the village) or flights to Åre Östersund, plus transfers

activities.note: Lift passes roughly €55-70 per day, €270-330 for six days; guided off-piste €150-250; heliskiing where operating, considerably more

summary: A seven-day winter sports & skiing itinerary in Jämtland, central Sweden, Sweden.

itinerary.title: Night train to Åre
itinerary.morning: Arrive on the overnight train from Stockholm, which pulls in at Åre station in the middle of the village, no transfer, no hire car, boots on within twenty minutes.
itinerary.afternoon: Collect passes and gear. Ski the village-side runs off the Kabinbanan cable car to get oriented.
itinerary.evening: Åre has the best après in the Nordics by a distance, and it starts at 15:00 on the mountain. Pace accordingly.

itinerary.title: Åre By and the Kabinbanan sector
itinerary.morning: The main face above the village: long groomed reds, the World Championship courses, and the cable car to the mid-mountain.
itinerary.afternoon: Explore toward Tegefjäll on the connected lift chain. Åre's four areas are linked, but the links are lift-and-piste chains rather than a single ridge, learn the map on day two, not day five.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in the village. Åre's restaurant scene is unusually good for a ski resort and the village has a proper high street.

itinerary.title: Duved and Tegefjäll
itinerary.morning: Duved, the western area, is quieter, more sheltered and better in bad weather, its tree runs work when the summit is closed.
itinerary.afternoon: Tegefjäll's north-facing terrain holds snow well and is where locals ski on a powder day.
itinerary.evening: Sauna, then an early dinner. Swedish *afterski* is an institution but it is also a trap on a seven-day trip.

itinerary.title: The summit and the north face
itinerary.morning: If the wind allows, ride to the **Åreskutan** summit sector. The mountain top at 1,420 m stands alone above the Jämtland plateau and the view over the lakes is the reason the resort exists. The summit lifts close in wind regularly, take the window when it opens rather than saving it for later in the week.
itinerary.afternoon: With a guide, the north face and the Ullådalen valley off-piste. Without one, the long marked descent from the top to the village, around 6 km, is the classic run.
itinerary.evening: Buustamons Fjällgård or one of the mountain restaurants reached by snowcat or skis for dinner, which is an Åre tradition worth booking.

itinerary.title: Cross-country, or a rest day in Jämtland
itinerary.morning: Åre's Nordic tracks run along the valley and up onto the plateau. Jämtland is also Sweden's most interesting rural food region, a genuine artisan-cheese and charcuterie culture, with producers within an hour's drive.
itinerary.afternoon: Alternatively, Tännforsen, Sweden's largest waterfall by volume, 38 m wide, spectacularly frozen in midwinter and reachable in half an hour.
itinerary.evening: Cook in the apartment with what you bought from the producers.

itinerary.title: Big ski day: whole-mountain traverse
itinerary.morning: Ski all four areas end to end, Björnen to Duved, using the lift chain. It takes a full day at a steady pace and it is the best way to understand the resort's scale.
itinerary.afternoon: Finish on the village face; the last cable car down is a fixed time and it matters.
itinerary.evening: Last dinner, last après. Åre's bars in April, in daylight at 20:00, are a particular pleasure.

itinerary.title: Morning ski and out
itinerary.morning: A final two hours on the pass, then pack.
itinerary.afternoon: Night train south from the village station, or the drive to Åre Östersund airport (about 1 h 20).

accommodationStrategy.name: Copperhill Mountain Lodge
accommodationStrategy.description: A designed mountain lodge on a ridge above the resort with panoramic glass, a spa and a serious kitchen. Away from the village noise, ski access from the door, and the best architecture in Swedish skiing.

accommodationStrategy.name: Åre By village apartments and Hotell Åregården
accommodationStrategy.description: In the village itself, walking distance to the cable car, the station, the restaurants and the après. The right base if you came without a car and want to use the night train at both ends.

accommodationStrategy.name: Duved and Tegefjäll apartments
accommodationStrategy.description: Cheaper, quieter, family-oriented, and next to the areas that ski best in poor weather. Ski bus links them to the village. Best value for a group of four or more, and a shorter lift queue every morning.

logistics.emergency: 112. Åre has a medical centre; the hospital is in Östersund, about an hour away. Ski patrol is on the mountain during lift hours.
logistics.bookingWindows: Swedish sportlov (the February school ski weeks, staggered by region) and Easter fill everything 6-9 months out. January and early December are the value windows. Mountain restaurants like the snowcat-access lodges: 3-6 weeks.

other.label: Lift pass tiers
other.text: Åre is a SkiStar resort: passes are priced by duration with significant online pre-booking discounts, and cover all four linked areas. Multi-resort options exist across the group's Swedish and Norwegian mountains. Prices and structures change every season, check before buying. `verify: true`

other.label: Wind closures
other.text: The Åreskutan summit sector is the resort's signature and its least reliable asset. Ski the summit the first clear, calm morning you get. The lower and tree-lined areas, Duved and Tegefjäll, are the bad-weather plan.

other.label: Avalanche and off-piste
other.text: The north face and Ullådalen are avalanche terrain with real accident history. Sweden's avalanche forecast for the Jämtland mountains is published by the national authority; carry transceiver, shovel and probe, and hire a guide unless you are trained and equipped.

other.label: The night train
other.text: The Stockholm-Åre sleeper arrives in the village and is the single best way to reach a Nordic ski resort. Cabins sell out for the February and Easter weeks months ahead.

other.label: Alcohol
other.text: Systembolaget is the only off-licence, closes early Saturday and is shut Sunday. Åre's bar prices are Swedish-resort prices; buy for the apartment during the week.

proTips: Take the **night train** both ways. It saves two hotel nights, arrives at the lifts, and is genuinely comfortable in a two-berth cabin.
**Ski the summit the first calm morning.** Do not save Åreskutan for a planned day later in the week; the mountain decides, not you.
Book one **mountain-restaurant dinner** reached by snowcat or skis. It is an Åre institution and the ride back down in the dark is half the experience.
April in Åre is the underrated week: full snow base, 14 hours of daylight, spring corn snow in the afternoon, and terrace après in sunglasses.
Buy the pass online **before you travel**. SkiStar's dynamic pricing means the same pass can differ by 30% between an early online purchase and the ticket window.
If you have a car and one spare afternoon, drive to **Tännforsen** frozen, and buy Jämtland cheese on the way back. It is the best two hours you will spend off the snow.

raw.resort_profile: Sweden's largest and most complete ski destination: four linked base areas, Åre By, Åre Björnen, Tegefjäll and Duved, under the Åreskutan massif, with a genuine village, three Alpine World Ski Championships in its history, and the Nordics' widest terrain variety
raw.lift_network: Around 85-90 marked runs and roughly 40 lifts across the linked areas, including the Kabinbanan cable car from the village and the summit sector on Åreskutan
raw.snow_reliability: Good and long, with heavy snowmaking investment. The caveat is that Åre is a high-latitude but relatively maritime-influenced mountain, the exposed **summit sector closes in wind frequently**, and thaw-freeze cycles happen at village level in midwinter
raw.off_piste_terrain: The Åreskutan north face and the Ullådalen valley are the classic lines; both are avalanche terrain and guided access is strongly advised
